solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Intense interest grips crossword compiler of some renown (5)

indicators.note: one word grips another by holding it inside, so FAD closes around ME

blocks.note: a craze, a short burst of intense interest
the setter speaking of themself

annotation.surface: A famous setter finds a craze has taken hold of them.
annotation.walkthrough: The crossword compiler is the setter of this very puzzle, and a setter refers to themself as ME.
annotation.definitionFit: Famed and 'of some renown' both describe someone widely known.

entries.clue: Chance to leave impression following lie about mathematician (9)

indicators.note: DENT leaves ACCIDENT, leaving ACCI
following means coming after, so the leftover chance is written after the lie and 'about'

blocks.note: a fib is a small lie
on = about, as in 'a book on birds'
ACCIDENT, a chance, without DENT, an impression

annotation.surface: A mathematician tells a lie that leaves a lasting impression by chance.
annotation.walkthrough: A dent is an impression pressed into a surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Fibonacci was the medieval Italian mathematician of the Fibonacci sequence.

entries.clue: Gun man saying Rebecca used him? (5)

blocks.note: Hiram, the American inventor of an early machine gun that bears his surname
a pithy proverb or rule of conduct
Rebecca's husband, de Winter, in du Maurier's novel

annotation.surface: A gunman's catchphrase, which Rebecca used on him.
annotation.walkthrough: This is three definitions. In Daphne du Maurier's Rebecca, the dead first wife Rebecca manipulated her husband Maxim de Winter.
annotation.definitionFit: Maxim is the gun and its inventor, a saying, and the husband in Rebecca.

entries.clue: Ice fields on which bases are established (8)

definitions.text: fields on which bases are established

blocks.note: underworld slang for gemstones, as in stolen ice

blocks.clueFragment: fields on which bases are established
blocks.note: a baseball field is a diamond, with a base at each corner

annotation.surface: Ice fields where polar research bases are set up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ice fields' reads as a polar landscape. The split is after 'Ice', and the bases are baseball's.
annotation.definitionFit: Ice is underworld slang for diamonds, and a baseball infield is called a diamond.

entries.clue: Seize money from Cape Town banks using small keys found on me (4,5)

indicators.note: a bank lines a river on both sides, so BAG lines BY on either side

blocks.note: to bag = to seize or grab, split BA…G
by = using, as in 'travel by train'
the rand is South Africa's currency

annotation.surface: A thief grabs South African cash from the banks of Cape Town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests money in Cape Town's banks, but it is a container instruction. The definition speaks as the piano: a smaller grand with its keys on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A baby grand is the smallest kind of grand piano, and the keys are found on it.

entries.clue: Signal page with buzzer first (4)

indicators.note: BEE is placed first, before P

blocks.note: a bee buzzes
p = page

annotation.surface: Paging someone with a buzzer before anything else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' looks like a paging device, which fits 'page'; it is the insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short electronic tone that serves as an alert.

entries.clue: Old Peruvian liquor encapsulates “mind-numbing diversion” (5,5)

indicators.note: BRANDY holds INCA inside it like a capsule

blocks.note: the spirit, split BRA…NDY
the Incas ruled old Peru

annotation.surface: An ancient Peruvian drink that sums up a numbing pastime.
annotation.walkthrough: Brain candy is light entertainment that demands no thought.
annotation.definitionFit: Brain candy is undemanding entertainment, a diversion that numbs the mind.

entries.clue: Fouled up on sticky diet? (6)

blocks.note: made a mess of things: the definition, read plainly
read the answer as a compound: nourished on sticky stuff, like 'corn-fed'

annotation.surface: Someone messes up while on a diet of sticky food.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GOO-FED to see the diet.
annotation.definitionFit: To goof is to blunder, so goofed means fouled up.

entries.clue: Up to about five hundred crews embrace change (9)

indicators.note: AT goes about the rest, round the outside
the two lots of MEN embrace D between them

blocks.note: at = up to, as in 'up to the door'; split A…T
a crew is its men; the plural gives two lots, split MEN…MEN
D = 500 in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Nearly five hundred crew members welcome a change.
annotation.walkthrough: The plural 'crews' supplies MEN twice, one on each side of D.
annotation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change, especially to a text or law.

entries.clue: Put off weightwatcher wanting the tiniest serving of ice-cream (5)

indicators.note: DIETER is wanting, or lacking, the I
the smallest possible helping is one letter, the first

blocks.note: someone watching their weight
I, removed

annotation.surface: A slimmer refuses even the smallest spoonful of ice cream.
annotation.walkthrough: The dieter's refusal of ice cream is the whole picture; the ice cream supplies only its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean discourage someone from acting.

entries.clue: Still it produces German beers UK ale lovers put in report (3,6)

indicators.note: a report is a spoken account, so the words are to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: bock is a strong German lager
CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, the British real-ale lobby

annotation.surface: A report on British ale enthusiasts sampling German beer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'even so', but it is the noun: a still photograph. CAMRA is said 'camra', which is how many people say camera.
annotation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early camera, and a still photo is what it produces.

entries.clue: Shooting a plus score for the round, he’s out of the Open (5)

indicators.note: HE is taken out of THE, leaving T

blocks.clueFragment: Shooting a plus score for the round
blocks.note: a golfer with a plus score has gone over par
THE without HE

annotation.surface: A golfer shoots over par and is knocked out of the Open championship.
annotation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's British championship, which makes it look like the setting; it is the definition, with a lower-case sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden.

entries.clue: Left kill to accept title of Man Hunter (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue, going left means reading right to left, so DO IN turns round
NIOD accepts MR by taking it inside

blocks.note: to do in = to kill
the title Mr, used for a man

annotation.surface: An order to kill that also asks us to give a man-hunter a title.
annotation.walkthrough: Nimrod is the mighty hunter of Genesis, and his name became a byword for one. 'Man Hunter' reads as one phrase, but the split is after 'Man'.
annotation.definitionFit: Nimrod, 'a mighty hunter before the Lord', lends his name to any great hunter.

entries.clue: Produce notes making separate contributions to new degree (8)

indicators.note: each N goes in on its own, at a different place
DEGREE is made new, its letters rearranged

blocks.note: N = note, twice for the plural
rearranged to EGEDER, with the Ns slotted in

annotation.surface: Someone writes notes to contribute toward a new degree.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged DEGREE reads E_GE_DER, and each N fills one gap separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean cause to exist or bring about.

entries.clue: During dramatic interval, dance old mum’s parts (10)

indicators.note: MA'S parts ANTIQUE, splitting it in two

blocks.note: antique = old
MA'S, mum's

annotation.surface: Old mum dances her parts in the interval of a play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like roles in the drama, but it is a verb: MAS parts ANTIQUE as ANTI…QUE.
annotation.definitionFit: An antimasque was a comic or grotesque dance performed between the scenes of a masque.

entries.clue: Acting with caution around Sicily’s Madam White (10)

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for cautious is wrapped round the Italian madam

blocks.note: chary = wary, cautious
donna is Italian for lady or madam

annotation.surface: A cautious approach to a Sicilian madam called White.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Madam White' reads as a person's name. White is the definition, a white wine.
annotation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is one of the best-known white wine grapes, and its wine is a white.

entries.clue: Appear like Lent with a sad tear? (9)

definitions.text: Appear like Lent with a sad tear?

indicators.note: sad as in wretched and messed up, so A TEAR is jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, in letters 2, 4, 6 and 8
A TEAR jumbled to ATRAE, in letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9

annotation.surface: A mournful question about looking as Lent does, tearful.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is the answer itself: A-L-T-E-R-N-A-T-E alternates the letters of LENT with a jumbled A TEAR.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the answer's own spelling: LENT's letters take turns with those of a jumbled A TEAR.

entries.clue: Winning shot from majestic Djokovic? (4)

indicators.note: shot from means fired out of, so UP is shot out of the word for majestic

blocks.note: superb = magnificent, majestic
UP = ahead, winning, removed

annotation.surface: A tennis fan hails a winning shot from the majestic Djokovic.
annotation.walkthrough: The tennis scene makes 'Winning shot' look like one phrase. Novak Djokovic is Serbian; the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Djokovic is one example of a Serb, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Exploit with energy drink lands someone in the Tower (9)

indicators.note: BEER lands, or catches, E FEAT inside it

blocks.note: split BE…ER
e = energy
an exploit is a feat

annotation.surface: A heroic drinker ends up in the Tower of London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lands someone in the Tower' sounds like prison; a Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder, a ceremonial guard at the Tower of London.
annotation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the warders who guard the Tower of London.

entries.clue: Bones makes call tracking old vessel’s location (8)

indicators.note: to track is to follow, so RINGS comes after O

blocks.note: Bones is slang for a doctor; MO is a Medical Officer
o = old
to ring = to phone

annotation.surface: A doctor phones to find where an old ship lies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bones' is a nickname for a doctor, as with the ship's doctor in Star Trek.
annotation.definitionFit: A vessel's moorings are where it is tied up.

entries.clue: Enthusiastic about tagging along without wife (4)

indicators.note: IN TOW goes without its W

blocks.note: in tow = following along behind
W = wife, removed

annotation.surface: Someone keen to tag along now that the wife is not coming.
annotation.walkthrough: IN TOW loses W, the standard abbreviation for wife.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for keen on, as in 'she's really ___ jazz'.

entries.clue: Go round and round offensive bow maker (7,3)

blocks.note: to wind = to turn round and round
a sortie is a military attack, an offensive

annotation.surface: A dizzy, spiralling attack by someone who makes archers' bows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective but is the noun, an attack. The bow is not an archer's but the knot in a tie.
annotation.definitionFit: A Windsor tie is a broad silk necktie tied in a loose bow.

entries.clue: This’ll be spicy, let’s wait up (3,3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom, so NOT NOW turns round

blocks.note: 'not now' = let's wait

annotation.surface: A cook warns the spicy dish will take a while.
annotation.walkthrough: A wonton is a Chinese dumpling, often served in spicy chilli oil.
annotation.definitionFit: Wontons are Chinese dumplings, often served in a spicy sauce.

entries.clue: Perennial lover of lassie hidden in long grass (8)

indicators.note: JO is tucked inside MARRAM, out of sight

blocks.note: marram is the long grass of sand dunes
jo is Scots for a sweetheart, as in 'John Anderson, my jo'

annotation.surface: A lass's lover hides in the long grass, as he always does.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perennial lover' reads as one steadfast suitor, but the definition ends at 'Perennial': a plant that lives for years. A lassie is a Scottish girl.
annotation.definitionFit: Marjoram is a herb, and sweet marjoram is a perennial plant.

entries.clue: Designs ways to express average income (5)

blocks.note: the verb: intends, plans
arithmetic, geometric and harmonic are three kinds of average
the money one has to live on

annotation.surface: Someone devises ways to present average income figures.
annotation.walkthrough: This is three definitions; the middle one is the mathematical means, several ways of expressing an average.
annotation.definitionFit: Means are intentions, averages, and one's income.

entries.clue: Passenger’s vacuous reaction to cold city (6)

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so PASSENGER is emptied to its ends, P and R

blocks.note: PASSENGER with its insides gone
an ague is a fit of shivering

annotation.surface: A passenger reacts blankly to a chilly city.
annotation.walkthrough: An ague is a fever with shivering fits, an old word for the shakes.
annotation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic.

entries.clue: Grounds for clergyman and poet occupying single bed (5)

indicators.note: the answer occupies the words single bed

blocks.note: the last three letters of single and the first two of bed

annotation.surface: A vicar and a poet share a single bed, grounds enough for scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: Glebe is land attached to a parish for the clergyman's income, and poets use it for earth or a field.
annotation.definitionFit: Glebe is church land for a clergyman, and a poetic word for soil.

entries.clue: A time to abandon assault course (4)

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave, so A and T leave the word for assault

blocks.note: an assault is an attack
A and T (time), removed

annotation.surface: An order to break off the attack at the obstacle course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assault course' reads as one phrase, a military training obstacle course; the split comes before 'course'.
annotation.definitionFit: A tack is a course of action, as in 'change tack'.

entries.clue: Works by Van Gogh? Old Man captured in pieces (5)

indicators.note: PA is captured inside ART

blocks.note: his paintings are art; the question mark says he is only an example
one's old man = father, pa

annotation.surface: An old man is captured in a Van Gogh painting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old Man' looks like the subject of a portrait; it is slang for a father, PA.
annotation.definitionFit: Something apart is in pieces, as in 'fall apart'.

entries.clue: Most unusual assignment for knights to receive is not for commoners (9)

indicators.note: QUEST receives AINT inside it

blocks.note: knights of legend went on quests
ain't, the common non-standard form of 'is not'

annotation.surface: An unusual mission reserved for knights, not ordinary folk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not for commoners' seems to mean exclusive to nobles; it tells us 'is not' is written the way commoners say it.
annotation.definitionFit: Quaint means oddly old-fashioned or unusual, so quaintest is most unusual.

entries.clue: Student of poor classes, one out of place in stream (9)

indicators.note: I, one, is taken out of SITE

blocks.note: SITE, a place, without I (one)
taken as written
a beck is a northern English word for a stream

annotation.surface: A pupil from a poor school, one who is out of place in the stream.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Student of poor classes' looks like a child at a bad school, and 'stream' like a school set. It means a writer who studied the poor.
annotation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck wrote of the dispossessed poor, as in The Grapes of Wrath, so he was a student of the poor classes.

entries.clue: Laid bare, as Man is blind (5)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, so AS WE ARE loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: AS WE ARE, since we are Man, without its outer A and E

annotation.surface: A philosopher's line: stripped naked, mankind is blind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is humankind, so 'as Man is' is 'as we are'. 'Blind' here is the verb in 'eff and blind', to curse.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: 'effing and blinding' is cursing, so blind alone means to use bad language.
